co_beer_barrel_boulder.blurb: A large freestanding boulder on Flagstaff Mountain above Boulder, with a smaller block perched on top. The east side is a gentle slab, while the west face hangs over at the base. Eleven sandstone problems cover a wide range, from a few easy V0 lines and a slab descent up through the middle grades to a handful of hard V7 to V9 problems, so beginners and strong boulderers both find something. It sits just downhill from the busy Monkey Traverse lot, which keeps it well visited.

co_elephant_rock.blurb: A single, oversized granite block standing beside the county road a few miles north of Buena Vista, on the west side once you are through the tunnels. Climbers compare the rock to Joshua Tree and Vedauwoo. Eleven climbs wrap around it: five trad lines, four sport routes and two boulder problems, with most roped climbs in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, one easier line on the south side and a very hard route or two on the east. Bob's Rock sits just across the road.

_expect.name: Silver Cascade Slab aka Hesitation Slab

co_silver_cascade_slab_aka_hesitation_sl.blurb: A compact granite slab in the upper reaches of North Cheyenne Canyon, close to Helen Hunt Falls on the Colorado Springs side. Most of the eleven routes are bolted slab climbs, with a few trad lines, and the bulk of them fall between 5.6 and 5.8, with one 5.10 and one 5.11 for those after more. Footwork and balance matter more than strength here, and a few lines are runout. The surface gets slick when wet, so it suits dry days, and morning sun means early starts keep friction better in summer. A moderate ice climb forms below it in winter.

co_barn_block.blurb: A small sandstone block in the Pink Floyd zone of the Nine Mile bouldering near Grand Junction, tucked a short way down the footpath from the Main Boulder. It has a vertical south side and a slabby north side, with eleven problems that are mostly easy to moderate: a cluster around V1, a handful in the V3 to V4 range, and one standout V5. Landings are mixed, so bring pads and a spotter. The zone as a whole is quiet, shielded from the highway, and the canyon wall throws shade over it later in the day.

co_army_of_darkness_roof.blurb: A cave-like roof of fine-grained sandstone on the hillside at Rabbit Mountain near Lyons. The problems start deep in the cave and tackle the overhang, so this is mainly a place for strong boulderers: of eleven problems, most sit between V6 and V8, with a couple of V10-level lines and a few easier ones to warm up on. Holds are varied and the climbing is sustained and powerful. The south-facing hillside gets plenty of sun, which makes it a good winter objective, but damp sandstone from snowdrifts should be left alone until it dries.

co_berlin_wall.blurb: A small, steep granite cliff tucked into a nook in Lower Dream Canyon, off Boulder Canyon, sitting between Krishna and the Wall of Winter Warmth. Around eleven routes mix modern, well-bolted sport lines, many of them hard, with older trad and mixed-protection routes from the 1980s that run steep and sometimes runout. Reaching it is an adventure in itself, with a creek crossing that is easiest when water is low, so it suits experienced climbers more than beginners.

co_amphitheater_wall.blurb: A short, south-facing sport wall behind the outdoor amphitheater at Performance Park in the middle of Estes Park, a few steps from the main street. The eleven routes are one-pitch bolted lines, around 35 to 90 feet, running from very easy beginner climbs up to about 5.11, plus a single V4 boulder problem. Holds can be sharp and the ground at the base is concrete. The rock is good rather than superb, and the approach is only a short walk around the back of the amphitheater, which makes it a handy place to learn.
